History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient ate prawn soup at approximately 19:00 after work.
Onset of symptoms about 30 minutes after eating prawn soup with lips initially feeling weird at the left corner progressing to upper lip swelling.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Onset ~30 min after eating: lips “felt weird” (L corner initially) → upper lip swelling

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports lip swelling is getting bigger, pumping blood, and feels worsening.
Associated symptoms include feeling of throat swelling or closing, difficulty breathing, possible chest tightness, and dizziness.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Assoc sx: feels throat swelling/closing; “can’t breathe that well”; possible chest tightness; dizziness

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient had a prior similar episode about one year ago after late-night Chinese food while intoxicated, waking the next morning quite swollen with difficulty breathing.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Prior similar episode ~1 year ago after late-night Chinese food while intoxicated: woke next morning “quite swollen” + difficulty breathing

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is unsure of the trigger of the prior episode, possibly curry.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of peanut allergy since childhood with severe reaction around age 6 requiring hospital visit per patient recollection.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Peanut allergy (since childhood); hx severe reaction age ~6 w/ hospital visit per pt recollection

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Possible shellfish or prawn allergy associated with current episode after prawn soup.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Possible shellfish/prawn allergy (current episode after prawn soup)

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient was initially alone during the call and later had her mother present.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Pt initially alone; later mother present during call

Assessment.content: Suspected anaphylaxis after prawn ingestion characterized by lip swelling, breathing difficulty, dizziness, and history of food allergy.
Assessment.source_text: Suspected anaphylaxis after prawn ingestion (lip swelling + breathing difficulty + dizziness; hx food allergy).

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient was instructed to call emergency medical services (999) for suspected anaphylactic reaction and ambulance was advised.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Activate EMS: instructed to call 999 for suspected anaphylactic reaction; ambulance advised

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient was advised not to remain alone and to have her mother stay with her until EMS arrives.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Do not remain alone; have mother stay with pt until EMS arrives

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient was advised to take an available antihistamine immediately while awaiting the ambulance and to ask household for supply.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Take available antihistamine immediately while awaiting ambulance (ask household for supply)

Plan_of_Care.content: Urgent emergency room or hospital evaluation was recommended.
After discharge, follow up to arrange adrenaline auto-injector and allergy management was recommended.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: After discharge: follow up to arrange adrenaline auto-injector (“injections”) and allergy management

Follow_up_Information.content: After hospital discharge, patient should follow up to arrange an adrenaline auto-injector and allergy management.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: After discharge: follow up to arrange adrenaline auto-injector (“injections”) and allergy management

Physical_Findings.content: Patient reported increasing upper lip swelling.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Pt reported upper lip swelling increasing

Physical_Findings.content: Patient reported shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, possible chest tightness, and dizziness.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Pt reported SOB/difficulty breathing, possible chest tightness, dizziness

Review_of_Systems.content: Respiratory: patient reports shortness of breath and difficulty breathing.
Cardiovascular/respiratory: patient reports possible chest tightness.
HEENT: patient reports upper lip swelling.
HEENT: patient feels throat swelling or closing.
